about.title: Fountain Valley Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fountain Valley records traffic deaths each year alongside dozens of injury crashes along corridors like Brookhurst, I-405, Euclid, and Edinger. Behind every one of those public-record numbers is a family trying to make sense of a sudden loss. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents or heirs able to step in when there's no immediate family. These cases move on a strict two-year clock from the date of death, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity, like a city road agency, is involved. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects grieving families in Fountain Valley with an independent attorney who can evaluate the claim, explain what losses may be recoverable, and walk through next steps without added pressure during an already difficult time.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to spouses, domestic partners, and children first, then certain dependents or heirs. An attorney can clarify where your family fits before time runs short.

items.title: Tracking the Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that deadline is shorter when a government entity is involved. Early guidance helps protect that window.

items.title: Clarity on What Can Be Recovered
items.desc: Beyond funeral costs, families may pursue lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can explain how these are documented and valued.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Fountain Valley?
items.answer: Under California law, the deadline is generally two years from the date of death. If the crash involved a government entity or road, that deadline can be much shorter, so it's worth speaking with someone promptly. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can walk through the specific timeline for your situation.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California law prioritizes surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children as the first to have standing. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible. An independent attorney can review your family's circumstances to determine who qualifies.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened on a busy Fountain Valley road like Brookhurst or the 405?
items.answer: Public crash records show these corridors, along with Euclid and Edinger, account for a notable share of Fountain Valley's injury collisions, often peaking on Friday evenings. That data can help an attorney understand contributing factors, but each case turns on its own facts. A free consultation can clarify what evidence matters most for your claim.

items.question: Is this a lawsuit against LawProactive or the attorney I'm matched with?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't handle your case directly. We simply help match you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for your family.
